title: Fix tail-latency regression in prefill/decode fairness
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: During validation of the H100 tuned scheduler preset (balanced mode), perf-canary and a customer-repro workload showed a p95/p99 tail latency regression on mixed prefill+decode traffic with streaming enabled. The regression was most visible when a small number of long-prefill requests arrived while the system was already serving many decode-bound streams: decodes would intermittently stall behind bursty prefills despite the intended prefill/decode fairness.

Root cause: Our fairness logic uses a token-credit mechanism to prevent prefills from starving decodes. In the tuned preset we increased max in-flight prefill work and widened the prefill batch window. Under certain queue shapes this allowed prefills to accumulate "credit" faster than decodes could spend it (especially when decode batches were smaller due to streaming cadence). The result was a periodic scheduler pattern where prefills would run in large chunks, pushing decode scheduling back, creating tail spikes.

Fix: (1) Introduce a capped prefill quantum per scheduling tick (prefill_quantum_tokens) and enforce an upper bound on consecutive prefill ticks when decode pressure is present. (2) Add hysteresis to the decode_pressure signal to avoid oscillation when the decode queue temporarily drains between stream chunks. (3) Tighten the definition of "decode pressure" to include active stream count + time-since-last-decode for each route, rather than only decode queue depth.

Trade-offs / expected impact: This shifts the scheduler slightly toward tail protection at the cost of a small reduction in peak throughput in highly prefill-heavy workloads. In perf-canary on H100 (balanced preset, workload matrix buckets 2/3/4), we see p95 latency improve 6–14% on mixed traffic and streaming stability improve (fewer >2s outliers). Tokens/sec on purely prefill-heavy runs drops ~0.8–2.1% depending on concurrency. Throughput-first mode remains unchanged (this change is gated to fairness logic shared by balanced and default, but throughput-first still overrides with higher prefill quantum).

Regression coverage: Adds a deterministic scheduler regression test that simulates a long-prefill arrival while multiple streaming decodes are active and asserts an upper bound on decode gap (no decode stall > X ms at fixed simulated times). Also adds a perf-suite guardrail that flags a >5% p95 regression in the relevant H100 matrix slice when H100 profile is enabled.

Rollout notes: No config key changes required. Two new internal config knobs are added with safe defaults; they are only exposed through the profile pack (not public API). This unblocks re-enabling the H100 balanced preset in the canary pool.

Refs: ENG-4824 (H100 preset), ENG-4828 (perf-canary gates), SUP-29410 (customer latency spike correlation).
commits: scheduler: cap prefill quantum when decode pressure is present
scheduler: add hysteresis to decode pressure signal to avoid oscillation
runtime: add metrics for consecutive_prefill_ticks and decode_gap_ms
tests: add deterministic regression test for mixed prefill/decode fairness
perf: add guardrail check for H100 mixed streaming p95 regression
checks: buildkite/perf-canary (H100 mixed streaming slice): FAIL (initial run, noisy runner) -> PASS (rerun)
review_conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): The cap on consecutive prefill ticks makes sense, but I want to be sure we’re not regressing prefill-only batch efficiency too much. Can you add a quick note with observed tokens/sec delta and confirm throughput-first mode behavior? Also: the hysteresis threshold values feel a bit magic — can we document why these constants were chosen.

Marcus Reed (author): Added perf numbers to PR description (prefill-heavy down 0.8–2.1% depending on concurrency; mixed traffic p95 improves 6–14%). Throughput-first still sets a higher quantum and disables consecutive tick cap when decode pressure is false; only applies when active streams present. I also added docs/internal/runtime/scheduler-fairness-notes.md with rationale for hysteresis constants (picked to cover typical streaming chunk cadence + avoid 50–150ms oscillation window).

Lena Fischer (review): Can we ensure the decode_pressure signal doesn’t flap when decode queue depth is zero but there are active streams waiting on the next chunk? The new time-since-last-decode seems good; please ensure it’s per-route to avoid one hot route throttling all routes.

Marcus Reed (author): Good catch. Updated to compute decode_pressure per-route and then aggregate with a max; also adjusted active stream accounting to be route-scoped.

Kira Volkov (review): Regression test looks good. Can we make the bound less sensitive to machine speed? It currently uses wall clock.

Marcus Reed (author): Switched test to a simulated time scheduler harness (FakeClock) and asserts on simulated ms. Should be deterministic now.

Rina Kobayashi (review): Perf-canary gate YAML: please link the workload matrix slice and include a note on why 5% p95 is the threshold.

Marcus Reed (author): Added link to workload matrix bucket (H100, streaming, mixed seq-len bucket 3, concurrency 32/64) and noted the 5% threshold aligns with our existing latency gate policy for profile rollouts.

Neha Kapoor (review): From SRE perspective: please add a quick knob/mitigation note in the changelog in case we see this again in production. Also ensure metrics exist to confirm we’re not starving prefills.

Marcus Reed (author): Added consecutive_prefill_ticks, decode_gap_ms, and prefill_quantum_applied metrics; changelog includes mitigation (disable profile / set fairness cap to 0 via internal override) with oncall pointers.

Sofia Ivanova (final): Approved. Please make sure this is called out in the next H100 profile roll-forward note.

Neha Kapoor (final): Approved contingent on perf-canary rerun passing (looks green now).
release_notes: Fixes a scheduler fairness regression that could increase p95/p99 latency for streaming workloads under mixed prefill/decode traffic (observed during H100 profile validation). Adds deterministic regression coverage and additional scheduler metrics for oncall triage.
